_comment: Central configuration for all linelist pipelines. Paths are relative to the repository root unless noted. Update epi_linelist.data.files.raw_linelist or contact_tracing.data.files.raw_contact_tracing when new DHIS2 exports arrive. Update epi_linelist.nowcasting.analysis_start when the analytic window changes.

pii_columns._comment: Columns holding personally identifiable information. Each export is written as two files: <name>_names.csv (the full table, PII included -- handle as confidential) and <name>_ctsafe.csv (an allowlist of columns, safe to share). There is no longer a third 'no names' copy; anything that must not see PII reads _names.csv and drops these columns on load. Listed here once so every script and report uses the same list, rather than each keeping its own copy.

epi_linelist._comment: Steps 2-6 (aggregation, nowcasting, dashboard plots, residence mapping/report) moved to BDBV2026-Contact_Tracing_Analysis, which keeps its own pipeline_configs.json with the nowcasting/qc config those steps need. This repo now only runs step 1.

data._matching_input_comment: WHICH CONTACT TRACING DATA the matching steps read (name rarity, CT dedup, person candidates, person registry). 'combined' = every export, built by contact_tracing_pipeline/2b-combine-exports.R into combined/ -- the all-time data. 'latest' = the latest export only, which since 27 Aug holds ~4 weeks. Combined runs are named LINELIST_x__CT-COMBINED_<latest export date>.

matching._comment: Tuning parameters shared by the four matching scripts: epi_linelist_pipeline/2-deduplicate_linelist.R, contact_tracing_pipeline/3-deduplicate_contacts.R, identify_persons/1-build_name_rarity.R and identify_persons/2-build-person-candidates.R. These values were previously duplicated as R literals in two to four scripts each and kept in step by tests that regexed the source; they live here so the invariant is structural. THE DERIVATION OF EACH VALUE STAYS IN THE R, in the comment at the point of use — this file carries only what a key means, never why the number is what it is. Changing any value here changes what past outputs would have been, so every run records the block it used alongside its output.

score_weights._comment: THE TWO COMPONENTS OF A LINK'S SCORE OUT OF 1.0. score = name * name_score + corroborator * corroborator_score. Both components are themselves in [0, 1]. These two numbers are the intended tuning surface for the whole matching system, which is why they sit at the top of this block: everything below them is a threshold on a nats-scale quantity and is calibrated, while these are a stated judgement about how much a name is worth relative to everything else the record agrees on. They must sum to 1 — score_weights() in 0-setup.R errors rather than normalising, because a pair that quietly does not sum to 1 makes a score recorded on one run incomparable with one recorded on another. Started at 0.5 / 0.5 as a deliberate null hypothesis. Moved to 0.6 / 0.4 on 2026-10-03: the first clean run at 0.5 / 0.5 kept 1,691 contact-to-linelist links on a near-zero name score (median name weight 6.3) carried by field agreement alone, chaining into clusters of 206, 159 and 117 identifiers. Re-scored on that run, 0.6 / 0.4 halves the links (11,834 to 5,905), caps the largest cluster at 7, and against the 602 unanimous reviewer decisions of 23 September keeps 445 of 451 kept links while dropping 74 of 151 broken ones. 0.65 / 0.35 dropped 29 kept links for 21 more broken ones, so it was not taken. The 0.5 / 0.5 run is in person_matching/archive/clean-run-0.5-weights-2026-10-03/.

corpus._comment: Which corpus a script's token rarity is measured over. Everything now reads the pooled running table built by identify_persons/1-build_name_rarity.R before any deduplication — except 3-deduplicate_contacts.R, which has this switch because the choice there is genuinely open and was measured to matter. Its candidate pairs are already confined to ONE source case's contact list, so a shared common name is far stronger evidence than the pooled table's frequency implies; scoring against the pooled table with unchanged thresholds dropped 11 identical-name pairs under the same source case. That is a threshold problem, not a rarity problem — the fix is one shared rarity plus a threshold reflecting the blocking prior. "ct_internal" preserves measured behaviour until that recalibration happens; "pooled" is the intended destination. The full argument is in the script, above ctd_build_idf().

token_match._comment: WHEN DO TWO DIFFERENTLY-SPELLED TOKENS COUNT AS THE SAME TOKEN? Replaced a single Jaro-Winkler ceiling of 0.15 on 2026-09-23. JW normalises by length, so one fixed ceiling means 'a constant FRACTION of the name may be wrong' — a 9-letter token absorbs a single typo three times more easily than a 4-letter one. That is why the junk at the old boundary was all short (de/dieu, mbalisi/mbavu, bahati/batia) while the genuine matches lost by tightening it were all long (voctorine/victorine, tibalengwa/tibilengwa). What we actually believe is that a small NUMBER of characters may be wrong, which is an edit count, so the gate is now an edit budget that grows with the shorter token. Measured against corroborating fields (sex/age/zone/area/onset, all independent of spelling) over 8,179 token comparisons: the old JW gate kept 470 matches backed by 4-5 agreeing fields against 153 backed by 0-1, a ratio of 2.4; this rule gives 431 against 88, a ratio of 3.7. Adding the JW test back on top changes 7 comparisons of 8,179 and costs one real match (kalembu/kalebmu, 5/5 fields agreeing), so it is not kept. The WHOLE-NAME Jaro-Winkler gate (name_weight.global_max_dist) is a different test and is unchanged.
token_match._metric_comment: Edit distance counting an adjacent-character swap as ONE edit rather than two. Not plain Levenshtein: 16 borderline token pairs in LINELIST_01092026 contain a swap and 11 of them sit in pairs where 4-5 independent fields agree — katsuva/kastuva, ruth/ruht, ngokpa/ngopka. The repeating ts/st pattern looks like a systematic transcription habit rather than noise. WHY "osa" AND NOT "dl": stringdist offers two metrics that both get called Damerau-Levenshtein. "osa" (optimal string alignment) forbids editing any substring twice; "dl" (unrestricted) allows a character to take part in several operations. They differ only where one character would be transposed twice — CA to ABC is 3 under osa and 2 under dl — which on 4-12 character name tokens essentially never happens. But the Python reference in tests/reference/strings.py implements osa, and the two must agree EXACTLY or the port-versus-R comparison in test_name_score.py is meaningless, so the metric is pinned to the one both sides compute.
token_match._budget_comment: max_edits applies when the SHORTER of the two tokens is at most max_token_chars, first match wins, and the last entry is the floor for anything longer. 1/2/3 at 5/9/above was chosen on the measurement above. Known edge cases in both directions, kept here so they are not rediscovered as bugs: PASCIE/PACIENCE is 4 edits on 6 characters and is REJECTED though all five fields agree; lusingwa/luyangwa is 2 edits on 8 characters and is ACCEPTED though it looks wrong. Any rule this simple has both; this one has fewer than the JW ceiling did.

tokenisation._comment: What counts as a name token. Must be identical everywhere or the same name scores differently in different scripts. Defined ONCE, in name_tokens() in 0-setup.R; these values are its defaults, so a caller that does not pass them cannot disagree with the corpus the rarity table was counted over.

collocation._comment: Detecting tokens that travel together (`de`+`dieu`+`jean`) so their IDF is not summed as though independent. min_together is an occurrence floor as well as a ratio: a ratio computed on two co-occurrences is noise. Detection now happens ONCE, in identify_persons/1-build_name_rarity.R, over the pooled corpus and before either deduplication runs; every consumer reads the resulting table. 3-deduplicate_contacts.R previously applied no collocation at all — see the carve-out comment there, which refused CT-INTERNAL detection on measurement and noted that the pooled groups would be safe. It now reads the pooled ones.

name_weight._comment: How name evidence is scored. Values ending _mult are MULTIPLES OF log(N) for the corpus in hand: an IDF ceiling is log(N), so an absolute value would mean something different in every corpus. single_token_mult (0.76) is used only for the rarity bands on the review tiles: the point at which one token counts as very rare. (min_name_mult and strong_name_mult, the old name floors, were removed with the tiers on 2026-10-03: the link score alone decides which links exist.)
name_weight._score_comment: TURNING THE NAME WEIGHT INTO A NUMBER OUT OF 1, which score_weights.name then scales to its share of the total. The weight is a sum of log(N/df) terms, so it is evidence in nats -- a log-odds -- and the logistic is the map from log-odds to [0,1]: score = 1 / (1 + exp(-(weight - midpoint) / steepness)). It approaches 1 without reaching it, so no clamp is needed. Both parameters are MULTIPLES OF log(N) for the same reason every other threshold here is: an absolute figure in nats means something different in every corpus. Calibrated on all 73,359 compared pairs of LINELIST_20092026 against the share of each weight bin with 4-5 of its corroborator fields agreeing -- those fields are independent of spelling, so they are evidence about the match that the name score did not produce. That share sits flat at 2-6% (chance) from weight 0 to 11, then rises: 15% at 12-13, 29% at 14-15, 42% at 16-17, 50% at 18-19, 54% at 20-24. midpoint_mult puts the half-way point at that 50% crossing. NOTE the proxy is compressed at the top -- genuine duplicates disagree on some field, so the observed share cannot reach 100% -- and the fitted curve is expected to sit above it past weight 20. ALL THREE MATCHERS READ THESE TWO KEYS, but only the linelist's fit is measured. CT and the cross-file matcher use the same curve deliberately, as a placeholder: their weights are on the same scale now (one pooled corpus, one tokeniser, one token gate), so the same curve is at least coherent, but each has its own prior and its own corroborator denominators and should end up with its own midpoint. Splitting them means adding a per-matcher key here, not changing the function.

corroborators._comment: Agreement on sex / health zone / health area / age / onset: the corroborator half of the link score. Scored against the fields a given pair can actually compare (n_corroborators_available). (tier_a_frac / tier_b_frac, the old tier requirements, were removed on 2026-10-03.)
corroborators._score_comment: TURNING CORROBORATOR AGREEMENT INTO A NUMBER OUT OF 1, which score_weights.corroborator then scales. EVERY FIELD IS WORTH 1, which is a deliberate null hypothesis and not a measurement -- the same stance score_weights takes. It is known to be wrong in a specific direction: sex agrees by chance on about half of all pairs and is worth very little, while onset within a week is a real coincidence and worth a lot. The honest weighting is -log(chance agreement rate) per field, computable from each column's own distribution with no matched pairs and no reference to the name score, so the two halves of the total stay independent evidence. Do that once there is matching to tune against. Net evidence is agreements minus disagreements, 2*n_corroborators - n_corroborators_available: a field blank on either side is not comparable, is excluded from n_corroborators_available, and is therefore neither credit nor penalty. The logistic is centred on ZERO so that a pair with nothing comparable scores 0.5 -- neutral, the middle of the available half -- rather than being punished for blank fields. score_steepness is in units of net agreeing fields: at 1.5, one net agreement gives 0.66, three give 0.88, five give 0.97, and five disagreements give 0.03.
corroborators._denominator_comment: N_CORROBORATORS_AVAILABLE IS PER PAIR, AND WAS NOT ALWAYS. Until 2026-09-24 only epi_linelist_pipeline/2-deduplicate_linelist.R computed it that way. 3-deduplicate_contacts.R hard-coded 5 and 1 for its two passes, and identify_persons/2-build-person-candidates.R asked whether ANY record in each population carried the field. Both make the denominator a constant for the comparison type, and since an agreement test is FALSE on a blank, an ordinary missing value then landed in n_avail - n_corr exactly as a contradiction would. The sentence above was thus true only of a field absent from a WHOLE POPULATION -- a source case has no sex, ever -- and false of ordinary missing data, which is most of it. A contact-to-linelist pair agreeing on sex and zone with age and area blank scored 2*2 - 4 = 0 -> 0.50 rather than 2*2 - 2 = +2 -> 0.79, and a pair agreeing on the one field it could compare with three blank scored -2 -> 0.21: punished for what was never recorded. All three matchers now compute it per pair, with one availability term per agreement term, asserted by tests/test_cluster_rules.py. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEDGER: corroborator scores and link scores recorded before 2026-09-24 are not comparable with ones after it on the CT and cross-file sides. The linelist side is unaffected -- it was always per pair.

link_score._comment: THE ONE CUTOFF, read by all three matchers. A link scoring below min_keep is not written: it is not a weak candidate, it is not a candidate. Chosen by eye on the first run that produced a score for every compared pair -- 193,514 of the linelist's 220,606 fell below 0.2 and were single shared surnames in different zones, the band 0.2-0.4 was mixed and thinning, and 0.4 is where the examples start looking like people rather than coincidences. It is a judgement, not a measurement, and the measurement that would replace it needs labels the pipeline does not yet have. WHAT IT COSTS: the files no longer describe what lies below 0.4, so the curve underneath cannot be re-fitted from them -- the same circularity that made the old name floor impossible to calibrate against. Lower this key and re-run before fitting anything that depends on the shape down there. NOT A PER-LINK-TYPE NUMBER, though the ceiling is: a comparison with one corroborator field tops out near 0.83 where one with five reaches 0.98, so the same cutoff is a stiffer test for source-case links. Left flat deliberately, since those links carry less evidence and should clear a bar less often.
link_score._calibration_comment: auto_accept SET TO 1.0 DELIBERATELY, and temporarily. Nothing but exact_source_alert reaches 1.0 -- the strongest scored link observed is 0.9365 -- so only identical-identifier clusters skip review and everything else is queued. This is not a judgement that 0.8 was wrong; it is a pause on auto-acceptance while the review_sample block below collects the labels to choose a number with. Put it back to 0.8, or to whatever those labels support, once they are in.
link_score._auto_accept_comment: THE CLUSTER SCORE AT WHICH NO HUMAN OPENS IT. A cluster scores its WEAKEST link, so this says every link in it clears the bar. Replaced the eleven review buckets on 2026-09-23; the measurement is in identify_persons/README.md under 'what the tiers see that the link score does not'. On that run it accepts 455 clusters where the buckets accepted 2,036 -- deliberately far more conservative, because the buckets were accepting 195 clusters scoring 0.4-0.5 while sending 359 from the same band to review. ONE VETO SURVIVES IT: a cluster holding both a confirmed case and a non-case goes to review however well it scores, because that is a claim about the case count rather than weak evidence, and the score cannot see it.

review_sample._comment: A LABELLED SAMPLE, to calibrate the scoring against human judgement instead of against itself. Every threshold in this file so far was set against a PROXY -- the share of pairs with 4-5 corroborator fields agreeing -- which stopped being independent evidence the moment those same fields entered the score. Real keep/break decisions on a known set of clusters break that circle. STRATIFIED, NOT A FLAT SHUFFLE: 1,952 of 4,192 clusters have their weakest link in 0.4-0.5, so a uniform sample spends half its reviews in the band whose answer is least in doubt and returns ~50 labels above 0.8, where a wrong auto-accept costs most. per_band clusters are drawn from each 0.1 band instead, and population rates are recovered afterwards by weighting each band by its true size -- record the band with every label or that weighting is impossible. SEEDED so 'the first 500' names one defined set of clusters rather than whatever a given session happened to show; the sample is written to review_sample.csv in the run folder and the order is fixed there. `enabled` puts the review interface in BLIND mode: the queue becomes this sample, in this order, and the link score is hidden from the edges and the cluster chip. That is not decoration -- a reviewer who can see 0.43 before reading a name is primed by the number being calibrated, and the labels come back correlated with it. Set false to return to ordinary score-ordered review.

near_miss._comment: THE AUDIT OF WHAT link_score.min_keep THROWS AWAY. Added 2026-10-18. Pairs scoring at least min_score but under link_score.min_keep are NOT candidates and never become edges or clusters; each matcher writes them to a separate near_miss file, and 2-build-person-candidates.R draws per_link_type of them from each link type into person_candidate_near_misses.csv for the Algorithm Tuning tab. Reviewers judge each pair same / different there, and the share judged 'same' is the miss rate of the cutoff. The draw is by a hash of the link_id, not a seeded shuffle, so a pair stays in the sample from one nightly build to the next while it stays in the band -- judgements carry over rather than being spread thinly over a new draw each night. Every row carries the size of its link type's band, so a population rate can be recovered by weighting.

ledger._comment: How the link ledger (identify_persons/3-build-link-ledger.R) turns reviewer votes into decisions. Votes are read from person_matching/reviewer_history/ (one file per reviewer, every run). consensus_min_reviewers: when at least this many reviewers voted on a link with the cluster marked CONFIRMED, all made the same call, and no confirmed vote says the opposite, the ledger decides it (decided_by = reviewer, basis = reviewer_consensus) without a harmoniser. Votes in clusters marked UNSURE are not counted and do not block. Anything else waits for the Harmonise tab. Set to 3 on 2026-10-03; lowered to 2 confirmed on 2026-10-06. A single reviewer is never authoritative.

training._comment: The link training table (identify_persons/5-build-link-training.R): one row per human-judged link, with a surety score out of 1 and name-free predictors, for the link classifier in the BDBV2026-Link_Classification repo. vote_*: what one reviewer vote is worth -- kept or broken, in a cluster marked confirmed or unsure (any mark other than confirmed counts as unsure, as in the ledger). harmoniser_unsure: a harmoniser verdict of unsure (escalate is not a judgement and is left out). harmoniser_weight: a harmoniser verdict counts as this many reviewer votes. surety = weighted mean of the values. shared_phone_max_records: a phone number on more than this many alert_ids is treated as not personal (an investigator's or a facility's), so it neither matches nor mismatches. Agreed with Ciara 2026-10-31.

model._comment: The link classifier (BDBV2026-Link_Classification). enabled: 1 = the predict step runs after the training table and the ledger applies its 'accept' decisions at the lowest authority (decided_by = model, rank 1); 0 = the predict step is skipped AND the ledger withdraws every earlier model decision on its next run. Model decisions are re-made every night from that night's file, never carried forward. Started at 0 (off) on 2026-10-31 so installing the code changes nothing until it is switched on. version: which saved model in <repo root>/link_classification/models/ the predict step (6-apply-link-model.R) uses; a text name, so it is read directly rather than through match_param().

audit._comment: The daily audit (identify_persons/7-build-audit-sample.R): a random set of pairs nobody has voted on, shown to reviewers blind before the normal queue, shuffled so a reviewer cannot tell the samples apart. n_model_accept: links the link classifier accepted, at least min_within_linelist of them within-linelist (its weakest type, and in no review queue). n_model_review: links it scored but left for people. n_near_miss: pairs scoring 0.3-0.4 that never became links (checks the 0.4 cut-off). Agreed 2026-10-31 at 20/12/10/5; cut to 10/6/5/5 on 2026-11-01 to keep the daily queue short. The audit clusters go at the front of the Review Persons queue.

review_queue._comment: WHICH SET the Person Review tab queues. The pipeline writes all three into the run folder. 'sample' = review_sample.csv, in its fixed shuffled order, in BLIND mode (link scores hidden; this replaces review_sample.enabled = true). 'contact_tracing' = review_contact_tracing.csv: clusters holding a CT contact or source case, minus those whose only link is an exact source-case ID match. 'all' = every cluster with a link to judge (review_all.csv). The last two are ordered strongest-first with scores shown.

quality_checks._comment: Data quality checks on the DHIS2 exports (pipelines/quality_checks/, see its README). Outputs hold column names, counts and percentages only, never row-level data.
quality_checks._known_events_app_comment: Findings marked 'expected' from the Shiny Data Quality tab are appended here (with who and when), not to known_events.csv: that file lives with the code and would be overwritten by the next code install on the server. This one lives with the data, so it syncs to S3 like the rest. The checks read both.

columns._comment: rename_similarity_min: a column that disappeared and one that appeared are reported as a likely rename when their names, after stripping DHIS2 prefixes and accents, have similarity >= this (1 - edit distance / longer length).
columns._contains_comment: Also a likely rename when one name (same normalisation) wholly contains the other and the shorter has at least this many characters: catches labels that were extended, e.g. 'Date d'enregistrement' -> 'Date d'enregistrement du contact'.

contents._comment: Renames are checked against what the columns hold. Each column's profile is its type (date/number/text/blank), its share of blank cells, and -- only when storing them cannot reveal a person -- its distinct values: at most values_max_distinct values, each seen at least values_min_count times, each at most values_max_chars long, and the raw column name not matching values_exclude_regex (names, phones, addresses, coordinates). A rename is 'differ' if the types differ, the blank shares are more than blank_tolerance apart, or the stored values overlap (Jaccard) less than values_jaccard_match. Two columns with unalike names are paired as a rename on contents alone when their stored values overlap >= contents_only_jaccard and they share >= contents_only_min_shared values.

structure._comment: Stage 2 structure checks (2-raw-export-structure.R), all warnings -- none stops the pipeline. row_change: flag when rows change by more than this fraction from the previous export (and any drop in the epi linelist). blank_jump / blank_jump_critical: flag when a column's share of blank cells rises by more than this (critical columns: the stricter one). stale_days: flag when the export's newest date in date_column is more than this many days before the date in its file name -- per dataset: contact tracing registrations arrive in weekly batches (newest usually the Sunday 4-7 days back), so 7 there, 3 for the epi linelist. window_gap_days: contact tracing -- flag when an export's earliest registration_date is more than this many days after the previous export's latest (contacts registered in between can never reach the combined table). date_plausible_from: earlier dates are ignored as typos when finding an export's date range. Category values a data/maps/ table does not know: mostly_untranslated when they are >= untranslated_share of the column's non-blank cells (every export, until the map is fixed); otherwise unknown_category_values when values new since the previous export cover >= unknown_new_min_share. free_text columns are skipped (every new spelling would count). column_now_empty / column_now_filled: a column counts as filled when at least fill_min_share of its cells are, so a stray value does not flip it. value_maps: which data/maps/ table cleaning applies to which standard column (as apply_value_translations() / apply_contact_value_translations() do -- a test keeps the two in step); values not in the table are flagged.

metrics._comment: Stage 3 (3-metrics-history.R): a growing history of counts and shares in the cleaned data, and flags when a share jumps. age_bands: lower bound of each age band in years (last is open-ended). A share is flagged when it moves by more than share_jump (absolute, 0.10 = 10 points) AND a two-proportion z-test gives p < p_value -- against the previous export (share_change) and against the pooled previous baseline_exports exports (share_drift). Only alert_subsets are flagged: the day's new rows shift for real reasons (where the outbreak is) and would bury data problems; they are still recorded for the plots.

report._comment: The run report's Trends section (pipelines/report/pipeline_run_report.Rmd): one chart per entry, in this order, from metrics_history.csv (all rows). dataset: epi_linelist / contact_tracing (each export) / contact_tracing_combined (history starts 2026-10-27). view: lines (each category's share), stacked (shares stacked to 100%), counts (rows stacked to the total). Shares are always out of ALL rows, blanks included (contacts, for the per-contact contact tracing measures). measures: names from metrics_history.csv. The alert-type -> status-at-sampling Sankey follows the trends when sankey is true.

trends.title: Epi linelist: alerts by case classification and type of alert
Epi linelist: status at sampling, sex, age group, province
Contact tracing (each export): follow-up result, age group

critical_columns._comment: A critical column missing from the LATEST export stops the pipeline (1-raw-export-columns.R). Present when any column's standard name (the name cleaning gives it) is in standard_names, or its raw name matches raw_regex. Health zone comes from splitting the org-unit hierarchy column, so that column stands in for it.
